title: Aluminum Cut-to-Size Tolerance: What Nine Suppliers Actually Publish
summary: OnlineMetals publishes plus or minus 0.125 inch. Speedy Metals publishes plus or minus 0.030 inch. Six other suppliers publish nothing. Here is every published cut tolerance and how much facing stock to leave.
body_markdown:
### What is a typical cut tolerance for aluminum plate?


Published figures range from plus or minus 0.030 inch on production sawing at Speedy Metals to plus or minus 0.125 inch on long and sheet products at OnlineMetals.com. Most suppliers publish nothing. Plan on plus or minus 0.060 inch or worse on a sawn edge unless you have a written commitment.


### How much material should I leave for facing on a cut-to-size plate?


Leave roughly twice the published tolerance per cut face, so 0.060 inch against a plus or minus 0.030 inch commitment and about 0.160 inch against plus or minus 0.125 inch. Add another 0.060 inch for thick sections above 3 inches and for stress-sensitive 7000-series material.


### Can I use a sawn edge as a reference surface?


No. A saw cut is a stock removal operation, not a finishing operation, and the edge will not be flat, square, or repeatable enough to serve as a datum. Face it before you use it as a reference.


### Why does thickness affect cut accuracy?


A saw blade deflects over the depth of the cut, and the deflection accumulates. Cutting 4 inches of 7075 gives the blade far more opportunity to wander than cutting 0.5 inch of 6061. Internal stress in thick 7000-series plate can also cause the material to move as it is cut.


### What is kerf and does it come out of my dimension?


Kerf is the material the blade removes as it cuts. Our bandsaws run a 0.08 inch kerf. Kerf is a layout consideration rather than a tolerance, but you should always confirm with any supplier whether the dimension you give them is the finished size or the layout size.
